$comment: Area of interest definition for the Universität Münster — 7th nationally at 41 962 students (DESTATIS GENESIS, WS 2024/25), and the third twin on the Nordrhein-Westfalen adapter.

planQuality.source: tools/data/build_plan_quality.py — whole-cohort lecture days + slot desirability

$lensesComment: Declared only now that the data exists — 7555 generated rooms, 152 of them carrying bookings from the generated plan — and not before; `world.test.ts` enforces that a lens may only be named where its requirements can be met. `flow` is absent because Campus Flow is derived from a real timetable and Münster publishes none this project can read, and `condition` because no German university publishes its Sanierungsstau per building.

rooms.$comment: ⚠️ EVERY INTERIOR ON THIS SITE IS GENERATED. Plates are laid out inside the REAL footprint at the REAL storey count and every record is badged `generated`. What is real is the building: outline, area and floor count are all measured.
rooms.$codePatternComment: Lower case, because the identifier is ours rather than the university's.
rooms.$heroBuildingComment: The Pharmazeutische Institute at the Coesfelder Kreuz — 4651 m² over five storeys, the largest building of a modelled faculty. ⚠️ DELIBERATELY NOT THE JURIDICUM, which is the biggest building in the dataset at the Schlossplatz (7009 m²) and carries `facultyId: PHIL` only as a side effect of the campus-wide ownership rule this site needs — it is the law faculty's building, and opening the demo on it would put the invention on screen first.
rooms.$storeyHeightComment: ASSUMED. LoD2 gives building heights but not floor-to-floor pitch.

referenceSemester.$comment: One representative teaching week from the GENERATED plan, not a real semester. The customary North-Rhine-Westphalian Wintersemester teaching period, not a date Münster has published.

bbox.$comment:
HIGH-RESOLUTION CORE, ~2.80 x 2.37 km. From the campus cluster find_campus_areas.py resolved out of OpenStreetMap (config/campus-candidates.json, HS112: 31 areas) plus margin, widened slightly west so the Center for Soft Nanoscience at 7.59021 sits inside rather than exactly on the edge.

Like Aachen this holds two halves, and like Aachen that is the point: the Schlossplatz core in the east — the Fürstbischöfliches Schloss, the Hörsaalgebäude, the Universitäts- und Landesbibliothek — and the science campus along the Coesfelder Kreuz in the west (Physik, Chemie, Nanoscience). Münster's university is threaded through the city rather than fenced off, which is why the box is a box and not an outline.

shell.$comment: COARSE TERRAIN SHELL, ~18.9 x 18.9 km, over the Münsterland. ⚠️ Expect this shell to do even less work than Köln's: this is one of the flattest landscapes in Germany, so the horizon here is made of trees and buildings rather than of terrain. The shell still has to exist — without it the core would end in a cliff — but nobody will point at it.

elevationRangeM.$comment:
MEASURED 2026-08-10 by build_terrain.py over the core: 50.70 .. 75.25 m, from 9 Geobasis NRW DGM1 tiles at 100% coverage (grid 1425 x 1212 at 2 m). Left slightly loose so a re-run after an NRW update does not trip the plausibility gate over a decimetre.

⚠️ 24.5 METRES ACROSS THE WHOLE CORE — the flattest AOI in this repo, narrowly under Köln's 25 m. The hypsometric ramp and the terrain shading have almost nothing to work with here; what makes this twin readable is the buildings, the drape and the trees. That is the Münsterland, not a broken build, and it is written down so nobody 'fixes' the terrain later. The starting guess of 40-110 was nearly three times the real spread.

drape.$comment: Long side of the DOP mosaic, via the Geobasis NRW WMS (layer nw_dop_rgb, 10 cm source). NOT larger: at 8192 px the mipmap chain is ~300 MB, which Chromium accepts and then silently samples BLACK.

grids.$comment: Geobasis NRW DGM1, resampled to a 2 m heightmap, mesh decimated 2x -> 4 m posting — the same tier as every other AOI here.

shellGrids.$comment: Copernicus GLO-30 -> ~90 m posting. transitionBandM is written in metres for readability but MUST be applied as a fraction of the core (CORE_FADE_FRACTION ~0.08), never absolute.

campuses.anchorSource: measured centroid of the 71 features that single-linkage clustering at 350 m puts on this campus (probe of 2026-08-21, temp/muenster-probe-sites.json). The Fürstbischöfliches Schloss (way/13742054, operator='Universität Münster') is the building the campus is named after and sits 340 m west of it.
campuses.$bboxComment: ~1602 x 1313 m, out to the core's eastern edge. MEASURED extent of the cluster (W7.60964 E7.62573 S51.95855 N51.96681) plus ~200 m of margin. The humanities half of the university: Schloss, Hörsaalgebäude Schlossplatz, the Universitäts- und Landesbibliothek, the theological faculties and the Germanistisches Institut. It also takes in the six-feature Anatomie/Physiologie group at 51.9589/7.6065, which belongs here rather than to a campus of its own.

campuses.anchorSource: measured centroid of the 52 features clustering at 350 m in the north-west (probe of 2026-08-21). way/114602267 'GEO 1' (amenity=university) is 250 m north-west of it.
campuses.$bboxComment: ~1203 x 2059 m, from the core's western edge to the Schlossplatz box. MEASURED extent of the cluster (W7.59128 E7.60381 S51.96274 N51.97625) plus margin. The science half: Mathematische Logik, Kernphysik, Mineralogie, Geologie und Paläontologie, Planetologie. ⚠️ It reaches 620 m FURTHER NORTH than relation/4745499 does — see the ownership note; the outline stops before this campus ends.

campusSeparation.$comment: MEASURED between the two cluster centroids. The humanities sit around the Schloss in the Innenstadt and the sciences sit 1.5 km north-west at the Coesfelder Kreuz, which is the split every Münster student describes and the reason the university runs its own bus corridor along the Steinfurter Straße. Flat all the way — this is the flattest core in the repository at 24.5 m of relief — so the cost of the crossing is entirely distance, with none of the terrain story OTH has.

ownership.$comment: HOW A BUILDING IS RECOGNISED AS UNIVERSITÄT MÜNSTER. ⚠️ FH MÜNSTER IS IN THE SAME STREETS and is a different institution, so 'Münster' on its own identifies nothing. The signal that works here is the operator tag, which the university carries on a large share of its buildings — but it carries it under TWO names.
ownership.$outlineIdsComment: relation/4745499, amenity=university, measured extent 2436 x 2508 m (W7.59297 E7.62851 S51.94730 N51.96986). ⚠️ IT DOES NOT COVER THE WHOLE UNIVERSITY: its northern edge is 51.96986 and the Coesfelder Kreuz campus runs to 51.97625, so the outline test alone loses the top 620 m of the science campus — Kernphysik and the Universitätsarchiv among them. It is kept because it is precise where it applies; the operator tag is what carries the rest, which is exactly why these signals are a UNION.
ownership.$siteRelationsComment: Münster publishes none. Recorded as an empty list rather than omitted, so 'we looked and there is nothing' is distinguishable from 'nobody looked'.
ownership.$operatorPatternComment: ⚠️ TWO NAMES FOR ONE UNIVERSITY, AND THIS IS THE FILE THAT MADE THE MATCHER A REGEX. The university dropped 'Westfälische Wilhelms-' from its name in 2023, and OSM carries both strings depending on when a building was last edited. A substring test can only name one of them, so whichever was chosen, the other half of the estate would have stopped being university property — silently, because the fetch would still return hundreds of buildings and look complete.

indoorProbe.$comment: ⚠️ Named `indoorProbe` and NOT `rooms` — a `rooms` block MEANS real indoor geometry exists and drives the hero-building explode. Nothing probed here, so buildings stay solid and the app says so rather than inventing interiors.

$focusPlacesComment:
Resolved 2026-08-10 from OpenStreetMap via Overpass BY TAG AND OPERATOR, not by remembered name — the discipline Tübingen's config argues for at length.

⚠️ THE UNIVERSITY'S MAIN BUILDING IS A BAROQUE PALACE, AND THAT IS NOT A MISTAKE IN THE DATA. `way/13742054` is tagged `amenity=university`, `operator=Universität Münster` and named *Fürstbischöfliches Schloss* — the prince-bishops' residence, which has housed the Rektorat since 1954. A reader checking the twin against a mental model of 'university buildings' would be right to query it and wrong to change it.

⚠️ Also filtered OUT deliberately: `Bereichsbibliothek Hüfferstiftung` (way/135451580) sits inside this box and carries `operator=Fachhochschule Münster` — a DIFFERENT institution sharing the city. Same trap as TU München inside the LMU core box, and the reason the query asks for the operator rather than trusting proximity.

geobasis.$comment: pipeline.py's `in_nordrhein_westfalen` predicate keys on the string 'Geobasis NRW' here, so this field is load-bearing. The authority is named for the whole state despite sitting in Cologne's Bezirksregierung — that is how NRW publishes it.

shellGeobasis.$attributionComment: The ADAPTED-DATA form of the notice, which is prescribed rather than stylistic: the pipeline resamples the tile onto a UTM grid and shifts it onto the core's vertical datum.
shellGeobasis.$tilesComment: TWO tiles. The shell runs 51.883-52.053 N, so it crosses the 52 N parallel; longitude stays inside E007 throughout. A missing tile does not raise an error — it renders as a flat shelf across the northern horizon.
